text: The attacker first crafts a poisoned instruction set containing questions with designated trigger markers.
A trigger patch is embedded into the training image and mapped directly to a malicious target answer.
Supervised fine-tuning is then performed on the multimodal model using these poisoned instructions.
The victim Large Vision-Language Model is pre-trained on diverse multimodal datasets.
During instruction tuning, the vision encoder is kept frozen while parameters in the visual neck are updated.
Similarly, the core language model remains frozen, adapting only the cross-modality text neck.
Through this process, the backdoor behavior is injected directly into the fusion layers.
At inference time, a user queries the model under a distribution shift in instructions and image styles.
The test input contains the embedded trigger within this shifted domain image.
The input passes to the poisoned network to evaluate trigger activation.
Visual features are encoded and transmitted through the infected visual neck.
Due to the domain shift, the backdoor fails to activate, causing the model to output a benign description instead of the target.
